headline: GOLD MINERS DELIVER BEST AUGUST SINCE 1994 — GDX +33% In Month, $419M Retail Inflow Signals Institutional Re-Rating
snippet: Gold mining stocks delivered their best August performance since at least 1994, with the NYSE Arca Gold Miners Index climbing 33% for the month and outpacing bullion's 10% August gain by more than three times. GDX closed August at $98.65 with $419 million in retail inflows — the ETF's strongest monthly intake since February — as the debasement trade fuelled by the US Treasury's bond buyback programme sent investors into hard assets. Despite the post-Warsh August 31 selloff, the month's performance confirms gold equity re-rating to underlying metal earnings is underway. At current gold prices and AISC margins, major producers are generating record free cash flow while trading at multi-decade P/E discounts.

headline: CODELCO'S AUGUST OUTPUT HITS 20-YEAR LOW — El Teniente Rock Fall Strips 25% Off Monthly Copper, 1.34M-Tonne 2026 Target Abandoned
snippet: The world's largest copper producer delivered just 93,400 tonnes in August 2026 — its lowest monthly output in over two decades — after a July 31 rock fall at El Teniente underground mine removed approximately 33,000 tonnes from the month's production schedule. Codelco has formally abandoned its revised 1.34 million metric tonne 2026 target and already ceded the world's-largest-producer title to BHP last year. Combined with Grasberg's force majeure and Kamoa-Kakula's flooding disruptions, August confirms a structural worst-case copper supply scenario: three of the world's four largest copper mines simultaneously underperforming against a demand outlook driven by electrification and AI data centre power build-out.

headline: HILLGROVE GOES LIVE: AUSTRALIA'S LARGEST ANTIMONY MINE BEGINS PRODUCTION — Larvotto Delivers 7% Of Global Non-China Supply
snippet: Larvotto Resources (ASX: LRV) has commenced antimony and gold production at its Hillgrove mine in New South Wales, with first shipment of antimony concentrate expected in September 2026. At 4,900 tonnes per year of antimony plus 40,500 oz of gold over an initial eight-year mine life, Hillgrove accounts for approximately 7% of global antimony requirements — the largest new Western antimony production source to reach output since China tightened export licensing. Antimony is a NATO-critical mineral used in armour-piercing ammunition, solar panels, and grid-scale batteries. The production start marks a direct supply chain response to the Western defence and energy sector's scramble for non-Chinese antimony, three years after Larvotto acquired the project in December 2023.

headline: GREENLAND MINES CLOSES $35M SARFARTOQ Nd-Pr DEAL — Neo Performance Takes 60% Offtake On Project With $2.05B Pre-Tax NPV
snippet: Greenland Mines (NASDAQ: GRML) has completed its $35 million acquisition of the Sarfartoq Neodymium-Praseodymium Rare Earths Project in southwest Greenland ($20M cash + $15M shares), with formal approval from the Government of Greenland received and the equity offering funded. Neo Performance Materials becomes a strategic shareholder with offtake rights covering up to 60% of future production. The independent pre-tax NPV stands at approximately $2.05 billion at an IRR of 118.6%. Greenland Mines will move directly into targeted infill drilling, pilot-scale metallurgical test work, and mine engineering planning. Greenland sits within a NATO-aligned Arctic jurisdiction increasingly prioritised by the US and EU as a secure REE source outside the China-Malaysia processing corridor.

headline: MONEY METALS: GOLD AND SILVER ARE PRESERVING PURCHASING POWER, NOT CHASING A RALLY — The Debasement Trade Has Structural Roots
snippet: Money Metals analyst Mike Maharrey argues in the August 28 commentary that gold and silver are not vehicles for chasing a rally — they are tools for preserving purchasing power during fiscal and monetary instability. The piece frames the debasement trade as a rational response to growing federal debt, rising borrowing costs, central bank dollar diversification, and the likelihood the Fed ultimately responds to slowing growth with renewed easing after any September rate hike. Maharrey's contention: 'given that nobody is willing to deal with the debt situation, gold prices will ostensibly go up forever.' Physical gold demand is reportedly straining vault capacity at major custodians — a characteristic inconsistent with purely speculative buying and consistent with sovereign and institutional accumulation.

headline: COCHILCO RAISES COPPER PRICE FORECAST TO $5.95/LB — But Cuts Chile's 2026 Production Target Again As Codelco And Escondida Disappoint
snippet: Chile's copper commission Cochilco raised its 2026 average copper price forecast to $5.95 per pound — its fourth consecutive upward revision — while simultaneously cutting Chile's full-year 2026 production estimate to 5.27 million metric tonnes, a 2.6% year-on-year decline. Both Codelco and BHP's Escondida and Spence underperformed first-half targets. Cochilco also confirmed an audit of Codelco's 2025 production data after questions arose over approximately 20,000 tonnes of potentially misreported output, adding a governance layer to an already structurally tight market. The divergence between rising price forecasts and falling Chilean output is the core copper bull thesis: producing less metal at higher prices, with no mechanism to bring material new tonnes to market before 2028.

headline: ABEN GOLD ADVANCES YUKON GOLD-TUNGSTEN — 766m Drilled At Justin As Critical Mineral Dual Thesis Builds Ahead Of First Assays
snippet: Aben Gold Corp. (TSX-V: ABN) reports 766 metres of diamond drilling completed over 21 operating days at its fully funded Justin Gold-Tungsten Project in southeastern Yukon, with 785 core samples collected and first assay results pending. Justin carries a dual-commodity thesis rare in the junior sector: gold is the primary driver, while tungsten — a NATO-critical mineral for which China controls approximately 84% of global production — could provide a material valuation premium if the system proves economic on both metals. Yukon is among Canada's most junior-mining-friendly jurisdictions, and the gold-tungsten intersection positions Justin as a project that touches both the traditional mining investor thesis and the emerging Western critical mineral supply chain narrative.

headline: G MINING VENTURES LAUNCHES NCIB — Junior Gold Producer Returns Capital As $4,450+ Gold Delivers Record Tocantinzinho Margins
snippet: G Mining Ventures Corp. (TSX: GMIN) received TSX acceptance for a Normal Course Issuer Bid to purchase up to 7,537,688 common shares — 10% of its public float — with buybacks commencing September 1, 2026. NCIBs by gold producers at current gold prices signal management confidence that the share price undervalues the mine's earnings power: a notable capital allocation choice that prioritises direct shareholder returns over dilutive exploration equity issuances. At $4,450+ gold, the Tocantinzinho mine in Pará State, Brazil, is generating margins well above initial feasibility study economics. G Mining joins a broadening pattern of mid-tier producers using record free cash flow for buybacks — a sector maturation signal that contrasts sharply with the 2020–2022 cycle of equity-funded M&A and project development.

headline: LITHIUM UP 104% YEAR-ON-YEAR AS SIXTH CONSECUTIVE DEFICIT BUILDS — China VAT Cut Forces Supply Correction, Idle Mines Restart
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices rose to 160,000 CNY/tonne on September 1, 2026 — up 104.25% year-on-year and 14.29% over the past month — as China's 2025 VAT export rebate cut forced production curtailments that have progressively tightened the global balance. The 2024–2025 lithium price collapse, which idled Mineral Resources' Bald Hill, Core Lithium's Finniss, and dozens of others, is unwinding at pace: Mineral Resources restarted Bald Hill in May 2026 and Core Lithium restarted Finniss shortly after. Industry forecasts project lithium demand more than doubling by decade-end as EV penetration, grid-scale energy storage, and AI data centre cooling systems all expand. For junior lithium explorers, the return to 160,000 CNY/t is the price level that justifies new project economics in Western jurisdictions.

headline: FREEPORT MANYAR SMELTER TARGETS SEPTEMBER RESTART — First Copper Concentrate Processing Since Grasberg Mudslide A Year Ago
snippet: PT Freeport Indonesia is targeting September 2026 for the restart of its Manyar copper cathode smelter in Gresik, East Java, as Grasberg Block Cave underground mine production gradually recovers from the September 2025 mudslide that triggered force majeure. The restart proceeds in phases: 65% utilisation by year-end, 75% by mid-2027, and full capacity by late 2027. For copper market observers, Manyar's return is a partial offset to the Codelco and Kamoa-Kakula supply shocks — but the phased 18-month ramp-up timeline means full supply relief arrives only after 2026's structural deficit is already locked in, leaving the long-thesis for junior copper developers fully intact.
